entries.title: Darkshore
body: A long strip of shadowed coast in north-western Kalimdor, named for the strange mist that blankets everything. Mountains shelter it from Felwood to the east; between them and the grey beaches lies a forest of evergreens that thickens southward into Ashenvale.

The night elves have mostly shunned it. Many tried to settle the land and failed, and Auberdine is their only real town. Ruins of the old Highborne crumble on its cliffs, haunted by ghosts and infested with naga, satyrs and grell, and even the sea is unsafe. It was from here that Fandral Staghelm led the druids to grow Teldrassil, which rises out of the sea on the western horizon.

entries.title: Auberdine
body: A night elven town on the shore of the Veiled Sea, the main port of the Alliance in northern Kalimdor. Its low, arched wooden buildings, lamplit bridges and stone streets sit among hills and pine forests, under a damp sky of near-constant storm clouds, with a lighthouse of elven design over the harbour.

Ships from the Eastern Kingdoms call here, so Auberdine is where the night elves trade with the outside world, and its people include dwarves, gnomes and humans as well as kaldorei. The Last Haven Tavern is its gathering place, and Thundris Windweaver serves as its elder.

entries.title: Ameth'Aran
body: The ruins of one of the twin towns Queen Azshara built for her favoured Highborne. Its servants practised their powerful magic freely here, among bazaars and temples to Elune.

In the War of the Ancients the town was destroyed, and its people perished, or worse. Now the restless spirits of the Highborne walk its broken streets, still wielding their ancient magic. Two great tablets in the ruins tell the story of the town and its fall.

entries.title: Bashal'Aran
body: The ruins of the second of Azshara's twin towns, south-west of Auberdine. Demons and their minions have moved in, satyrs and grell who feed on the magical energies still lingering in the stones and grow stronger the longer they stay.
They never approach one shrine, which glows with a strange blue aura. Within it, held by a moonstone seal, is the ghost of Asterion, the town's ancient protector.

entries.title: Tower of Althalaxx
body: A mage tower in northern Darkshore, some way from the twin towns, where their governor Athrikus Narassin spent most of his days once he grew bored of his post.

Ten thousand years later, a dark rumour about the tower proved true. A cult had gathered there, warlocks and a satyr among them, calling themselves the Cult of the Dark Strand, and Athrikus himself was its master.

entries.title: Ruins of Mathystra
body: A night elven city in northern Darkshore before the Great Sundering, utterly destroyed when the Well of Eternity exploded. The night elves abandoned it long ago for the smaller coastal villages to the south.

Relics of the old Highborne lie scattered among the stones, and young night elves sometimes go searching for them. The Stormscale naga have taken the ruins and guard them fiercely, and ghostly sabers prowl there.

entries.title: Cliffspring Falls
body: The source of the Cliffspring River and the main source of drinking water for the whole region. It was once a pure waterfall, but the cave it springs from has become corrupted.
Some believe the taint is seeping from nearby Felwood. Others blame the Twilight's Hammer, whose cultists have been found deep in the caves, among naga.

entries.title: Cliffspring River
body: The river that runs from Cliffspring Falls to the sea in northern Darkshore. It is tainted, and the animals that drink from it fall sick. Auberdine's elder fears the corruption will reach the town itself, and that it is the same taint he has seen come out of Felwood before.

entries.title: Grove of the Ancients
body: The sacred ruin of an old night elven temple in south-eastern Darkshore, built around the rushing Wildbend River near the mountains. The Circle of Ancients meets here, and Onu, an Ancient of Lore, lives among its stones with a sleeping druid and a pair of merchants.
It was here that Fandral Staghelm persuaded the Circle of Ancients that the time had come to grow a new World Tree.

entries.title: The Master's Glaive
body: A massive adamantine glaive in south-western Darkshore, embedded in the skull of Soggoth the Slitherer, a herald of the Old Gods. Onu calls it the place where an "old, old lord of the earth" fell.
It was once a night elven holy place. Now the Twilight's Hammer has come to dig up Soggoth's remains, meaning to bring him back to life.

entries.title: Remtravel's Excavation
body: An Explorers' League dig site named after the famous, and famously absent-minded, archaeologist Prospector Remtravel. It was here that the League found the tablets that tell the story of the Master's Glaive, and an unusual fossil with mystic properties.
As at so many League digs, the excavation woke what was buried: Gravelflint troggs and huge golems now hold it.

entries.title: Blackwood Den
body: A few camps and a small cave in the far south of Darkshore, near the Ashenvale border, held by the furbolgs of the Blackwood tribe. The tribe has been corrupted, like the furbolgs of Teldrassil and Felwood, and the night elves who live up-river from Auberdine suspect it of poisoning the waters.

entries.title: Mist's Edge and the Long Wash
body: Mist's Edge is by far the longest stretch of Darkshore's coast: gloomy bays and grey beaches dotted with sunken wrecks and littered with the huge carcasses of sea creatures. South of Auberdine the Long Wash, ironically the shortest stretch, is just as desolate.
The great turtles and threshers of the Veiled Sea have been fleeing the waters around Teldrassil to beach themselves and die here. Murlocs and crabs scuttle along the whole shore.

entries.title: Thundris Windweaver
body: The elder of Auberdine, well respected in the town, who offers sage and just stewardship of its daily affairs. He is an old friend of Huntress Kella Nightbow.
Thundris worries about the old Highborne magic still lingering in the ruins and wants its relics destroyed. He has seen Felwood's taint before, and fears it is reaching the rivers that feed his town.

entries.title: Onu
body: An Ancient of Lore, a member of the Circle of Ancients, known for his patience and wisdom. He awaits word from Fandral Staghelm on Teldrassil's growth, and finds the archdruid always in a hurry, unlike Malfurion.
Onu is troubled by the naga and the Twilight's Hammer in his land, and studies old relics from Mathystra to learn what the cult intends.

entries.title: Asterion
body: Ten thousand years ago, Asterion was second to Athrikus Narassin, a mage known for his arcane skill as much as his physical prowess. He lived among the people of Bashal'Aran and often went to Ameth'Aran to see to their needs.

For reasons no one knows, Athrikus made a moonstone seal and imprisoned him by magic in the ruins of Bashal'Aran. He lived a long, painful life there, and when he died he found, to his horror, that even as a ghost he was still a prisoner.

entries.title: Athrikus Narassin
body: One of Queen Azshara's most loyal servants, an aristocrat who prided himself on the magical items he collected and made, and the governor of the twin towns. In the War of the Ancients he was near the Well of Eternity when it exploded; the blast threw him far away, stripped him of his treasures, and made him immortal, able to drain the power of other mages to feed his own.

As the Sundering approached, he came to the survivors of Ameth'Aran and promised to save them. He trapped their souls in his soul gems, "life eternal", and used them to fuel his own power. Ten thousand years later he still lives, in the Tower of Althalaxx.

entries.title: Cerellean Whiteclaw
body: A druid who loved Anaya Dawnrunner of Ameth'Aran before the War of the Ancients. When the war left her city in ruins, Anaya was among the dead.

In sorrow, Cerellean followed Malfurion into the long hibernation, but his dreams were haunted by her. When he woke after thousands of years he wandered Auberdine in a daze, and found her spirit still haunting the ruins of her home. He knows it must be set free, and cannot bring himself to do it.

entries.title: The Twin Towns
body: Of all the towns built on the old lakeshore of north-western Kalimdor, Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran were the foremost, made by Azshara's own hand for her favoured Highborne. Athrikus Narassin governed them from his tower, and his second, Asterion, cared for their people.

The War of the Ancients ended them. When the Well of Eternity was shattered, the towns were destroyed, and their people either died, or accepted Athrikus' offer of eternal life inside his soul gems. Their ghosts remain.

entries.title: Kronn and Soggoth
body: Tablets found at Remtravel's Excavation tell of an ancient battle. Soggoth the Slitherer, a herald of the Old Gods, fought no fewer than twenty stone giants sent by the titans, and only the largest, Kronn, survived.

Kronn let himself be caught in Soggoth's tendrils just long enough to be lifted within reach of the creature's skull, and drove his sword into it. That sword is the Master's Glaive, and it has stood in Soggoth's skull ever since.

entries.title: The Taint from Felwood
body: Over the mountains lies Felwood, once a forest of Ashenvale, poisoned by the demons of the Burning Legion. The mountains shield Darkshore from most of its taint, but not all: the Wildbend River is the Bloodvenom of Felwood come down the cliffs, and sickness has spread through Darkshore's wildlife and furbolgs.
The Cenarion Circle has been asked for help. The night elves of Auberdine believe the corruption reaches their water through the rivers, but fear the water is not its only source.

entries.title: The Cult of the Dark Strand
body: The Cult of the Dark Strand gathered at the Tower of Althalaxx under Athrikus Narassin: warlocks of several races, and a satyr among them. Why they assembled after ten thousand years was at first a mystery.

The truth was that the cult answered to the Shadow Council, the old warlock cabal that once ruled the orcish Horde in secret. Athrikus still held soul gems from Ameth'Aran, two of them guarded by satyrs in north-eastern Ashenvale.
